panels.title: Engine stopped (fraction of wall clock)
panels.description: Wall clock the engine was stopped. Two series per node. 'probe' is measured inside the isolate by sleep overshoot and works on any collector; it counts scheduler preemption too, so it reads slightly high. 'gc beans' is the collector's own pause counter, which Substrate registers for its Serial GC only: it is empty on a G1 node, and it is kept here because it is the only series that covers history from before the probe existed. Where both are present they should track within roughly 20%. #684 ran at 89% stopped: back to back full collections in an exhausted heap. One isolate hosts every room on a node, so this stops all of them at once. Sustained above a few percent is that failure returning.

panels.title: Engine heap used vs ceiling
panels.description: The ceiling is baked into the image as a percentage of the cgroup limit, so mem_limit is the knob. A live set drifting toward it is what precedes the thrash; retention grows with the union of decks a node has hosted (#703).

panels.title: Decision stages p99
panels.description: Where a decision's time goes. In the 2026-08 stalls decision_total and next_prompt were identical to the millisecond, placing the time inside Forge producing the next question rather than in the bridge, the submit, or state serialisation.

panels.title: Engine decision p99 by room shape
panels.description: Rules work between a seat answering and the next prompt appearing, split by seat count. A fleet-wide quantile hides this: measured over two days of captures, 4 seats ran a p99 near 2.9s and put 2-5% of decisions over two seconds, while 2 seats sat at 0.35s with none. Bot decision time is not the problem, it is about 0.75s at p99 in those same rooms. Read over 30m rather than 5m on purpose: a quiet window holding 15 decisions makes its single worst one the p99, which is how one decision between 2s and 5s once drew a 4.58s peak. Needs node 0.22.0 or newer.

panels.title: Slow decisions per 5m (count, not a quantile)
panels.description: How many decisions crossed 1s and 2s, counted. A quantile cannot show this: a game on 2026-08-25 put 12 decisions over 2s and 96 over 1s, and the fleet-wide p99 still read 0.24s because a dozen events sit far above p99 among thousands. Rare events show up in counts and vanish in percentiles. Any sustained non-zero here is worth opening the capture for; the matching game id is in the slow-decision log panel.

panels.title: Slow decisions (10s or more), with game id
panels.description: Every decision at or above 10s, named. The metric can say a node was slow but never which game, so finding one previously meant replaying captures by hand. Match a spike on the panel to the left against a line here, then pull the capture by game_id.

panels.title: Relay state handling p99 by seats
panels.description: How long the relay spends on one state envelope: folding the patch into the cached board, deciding whether a full board is needed, and handing it to the audience. Labelled by seat count because the node emits one envelope per seat plus an observer, so the work per decision scales with the room even when the engine's own time does not. This interval previously had no metric: replaying captures put a four-seat room at a p99 of 2.3s outside the rules engine against 0.27s for two seats, and seeing that meant subtracting engineMs from capture timestamps in a script after the fact. Compare against 'Engine decision p99 by room shape': engine flat while this rises is relay-side cost.

panels.title: Outbound socket write and backlog
panels.description: The last unmeasured segment between the engine and the player. The outbound channel is unbounded and the writer awaits the sink, so a client that stops draining applies backpressure and every later message queues behind it. Backlog is how many messages were already waiting when this one was written. A rising backlog with flat handling time means the cost is a slow consumer, not the relay's own work. Backlog is a count, not seconds; read it against the right axis.

panels.title: Player round trip (heartbeat echo)
panels.description: The player's own leg, on the relay's clock via the RFC 6455 pong echo. The only genuinely variable leg: it moves with geography, where relay to node holds inside a few milliseconds. No server-side work improves it.

panels.title: Player-side engines — one report per finished game
Games measured
panels.description: Engine reports in the selected range. One per finished game, from the client that ran it: the relay files reports for a room it knows about, the hub takes offline play.

targets.queryText: SELECT count(*) AS games FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT count(*) AS games FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000

panels.title: Reporting engines
panels.description: How many distinct engines reported. 'forge-wasm' is Forge in the browser, 'forge-hosted' the node fleet, 'forge-desktop' the desktop app, 'manabrew' the Rust engine on the player's machine.

targets.queryText: SELECT count(DISTINCT engine) AS engines FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT count(DISTINCT engine) AS engines FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000

panels.title: forge-wasm p50
panels.description: Median across games of each game's p50 turnaround on forge-wasm. Turnaround is measured on the client: answer sent to next prompt on screen, so it carries the network for a hosted engine and nothing but the engine for a local one.

targets.queryText: WITH r AS (SELECT turnaround_p50 AS v, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn, count(*) OVER () AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE engine = 'forge-wasm' AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT round(avg(v)) AS p50_ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
targets.rawQueryText: WITH r AS (SELECT turnaround_p50 AS v, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn, count(*) OVER () AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE engine = 'forge-wasm' AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT round(avg(v)) AS p50_ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)

panels.title: Last report age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest engine report reached the analytics database. Reports arrive when games end and the ingester runs every five minutes, so quiet hours read high; hours of silence during play means the pipeline broke.

targets.queryText: SELECT strftime('%s', 'now') - coalesce((SELECT max(strftime('%s', ts)) FROM engine_stats), 0) AS seconds
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT strftime('%s', 'now') - coalesce((SELECT max(strftime('%s', ts)) FROM engine_stats), 0) AS seconds

panels.title: Turnaround p50 by engine (daily median)
panels.description: The wait a player feels between answering and being asked the next question. Each game contributes its own p50; the line is the median of those across the day, so one bad game cannot move it.

targets.queryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p50 AS v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, engine, round(avg(v)) AS ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY t, engine ORDER BY t, engine
targets.rawQueryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p50 AS v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, engine, round(avg(v)) AS ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY t, engine ORDER BY t, engine

panels.title: Turnaround p90 by engine (daily median)
panels.description: The same measure at each game's p90: the slow tenth of decisions, which is where a stalling engine shows up first.

targets.queryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p90 AS v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p90) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, engine, round(avg(v)) AS ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY t, engine ORDER BY t, engine
targets.rawQueryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p90 AS v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p90) AS rn, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, engine, round(avg(v)) AS ms FROM r WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) GROUP BY t, engine ORDER BY t, engine

panels.title: Engines compared
panels.description: Every engine and platform that reported in the range. p50 and p90 are medians across games of each game's own percentile; worst is the single slowest decision anyone saw.

targets.queryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, platform, turnaround_p50, turnaround_p90, turnaround_max, decisions, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn50, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform ORDER BY turnaround_p90) AS rn90, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT engine, platform, max(n) AS games, sum(decisions) AS decisions, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn50 IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p50 END)) AS p50_ms, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn90 IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p90 END)) AS p90_ms, max(turnaround_max) AS worst_ms FROM r GROUP BY engine, platform ORDER BY games DESC
targets.rawQueryText: WITH r AS (SELECT engine, platform, turnaround_p50, turnaround_p90, turnaround_max, decisions, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn50, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform ORDER BY turnaround_p90) AS rn90, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY engine, platform) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT engine, platform, max(n) AS games, sum(decisions) AS decisions, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn50 IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p50 END)) AS p50_ms, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn90 IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p90 END)) AS p90_ms, max(turnaround_max) AS worst_ms FROM r GROUP BY engine, platform ORDER BY games DESC

panels.title: Games reported per day by engine
panels.description: Reporting volume, which is also the adoption curve for the browser engine. A client reports once per finished game with at least five decisions in it.

targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, engine, count(*) AS games FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, engine, count(*) AS games FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2

panels.title: forge-wasm: engine think time against turnaround (daily median)
panels.description: Only the browser Forge build reports its own think time, measured inside the worker from the answer landing to the next prompt being ready. The gap between the two lines is everything outside the engine: the worker hop, React, and paint.

targets.queryText: WITH r AS (SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p50, engine_p50, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn_turn, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts) ORDER BY engine_p50) AS rn_think, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE engine = 'forge-wasm' AND engine_p50 IS NOT NULL AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn_turn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p50 END)) AS turnaround_p50, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn_think IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN engine_p50 END)) AS engine_think_p50 FROM r GROUP BY t ORDER BY t
targets.rawQueryText: WITH r AS (SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(ts)) AS INTEGER) AS t, turnaround_p50, engine_p50, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts) ORDER BY turnaround_p50) AS rn_turn, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts) ORDER BY engine_p50) AS rn_think, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY date(ts)) AS n FROM engine_stats WHERE engine = 'forge-wasm' AND engine_p50 IS NOT NULL AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000) SELECT t, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn_turn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN turnaround_p50 END)) AS turnaround_p50, round(avg(CASE WHEN rn_think IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2) THEN engine_p50 END)) AS engine_think_p50 FROM r GROUP BY t ORDER BY t

panels.title: Client versions reporting
panels.description: Which builds the reports came from. Desktop installs update only when the player relaunches, so a just-shipped measurement change is never everywhere at once.

targets.queryText: SELECT client_version, platform, engine, count(*) AS games, round(avg(duration_s) / 60.0, 1) AS avg_minutes FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY client_version, platform, engine ORDER BY games DESC
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT client_version, platform, engine, count(*) AS games, round(avg(duration_s) / 60.0, 1) AS avg_minutes FROM engine_stats WHERE CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', ts) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY client_version, platform, engine ORDER BY games DESC

panels.title: Games with a player, and how many of them reported
panels.description: The denominator for everything above. A client reports once per finished game with at least five decisions in it, so the two lines never meet — but a wide, persistent gap means reports are being lost, not that games are short. Games with only bots in them are excluded; they have no client to report. Reports that reach the hub instead of the relay carry no game id and cannot be joined, so they count in the panels above and not here.

targets.queryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(g.started_at)) AS INTEGER) AS t, count(*) AS "games with a player", sum(CASE WHEN s.game_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "games reported" FROM games g LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT game_id FROM engine_stats WHERE game_id IS NOT NULL) s ON s.game_id = g.game_id WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM game_players p WHERE p.game_id = g.game_id AND p.is_bot = 0) AND CAST(strftime('%s', g.started_at) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', g.started_at) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
targets.rawQueryText: SELECT CAST(strftime('%s', date(g.started_at)) AS INTEGER) AS t, count(*) AS "games with a player", sum(CASE WHEN s.game_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS "games reported" FROM games g LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT game_id FROM engine_stats WHERE game_id IS NOT NULL) s ON s.game_id = g.game_id WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM game_players p WHERE p.game_id = g.game_id AND p.is_bot = 0) AND CAST(strftime('%s', g.started_at) AS INTEGER) > $__from / 1000 AND CAST(strftime('%s', g.started_at) AS INTEGER) <= $__to / 1000 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Engine reports at the relay, by outcome
panels.description: What the relay did with the reports it was sent. Both drop paths are silent to the player by design: `outside_room` is a report that arrived after the seat was gone, `implausible` is a malformed or hostile one. Anything but `accepted` is invisible in every other panel here — the report simply never becomes a row. Offline games and games reported after the relay went away go to the hub and never appear on this panel at all.
